summary: Jawset Postshot is the desktop counterweight in this lane: a free-to-download Windows application that needs an NVIDIA card, keeps every image and every training step on the operator's own machine, and covers the whole path from a folder of photographs or a video to a trained radiance field that can be cropped, aligned, exported and dropped into Unreal Engine. It is scored here because it shows what the phone tools give up. It solves camera poses itself or imports them from COLMAP, Bundler or RealityScan; it reads professional image formats including raw and high-dynamic-range video, tracks the colour space through training and records it in the file; it will align a scene to a printed marker of a stated physical size, which is the only real-world scale mechanism found anywhere in this lane; and it writes its own non-standard metadata into the PLY header — colour space, anti-aliasing mode and world origin — because no splat format has anywhere to put them. Its export list is three items: a self-contained web page, lossless PLY, and SPZ with a version choice, and the reason given for keeping the older SPZ version is the honest state of splat interoperability — some third-party software does not read version 4 yet. There is no mesh, no time axis, no macOS or Linux build, and no statement of rights or authorship in anything it writes.

coverage.note: The application carries a full splat renderer with real controls over it — a minimum primitive radius, a harmonic degree used at render time, splat scale and opacity — separate from the training settings. There is no pass structure or render graph beyond the field itself.
